overview: We make your product easy to connect for people who do not write code. We build a connector for tools like Zapier or Make, with triggers such as new signup or new order and actions such as create a record. faq: Do I need a public API first?
You need an API or endpoints the connector can call. If you do not have them yet, our API Development service can build them first, and then we create the connector on top.
Will my connector be listed publicly?
We prepare it for the listing review and write the required text. Approval is decided by the platform and follows their rules, so we cannot promise acceptance or timing.
Who pays for Zapier or Make?
Each customer uses their own plan. You may need a free developer account to build the connector, which you create and own. We work inside it as a collaborator.
Can customers still use my API directly?
Yes. The connector is an extra door for people who prefer clicking to coding. Your API and its docs stay as they are, and both share the same sign-in.
desc:
Zapier and Make connectors for your product let customers link it to thousands of everyday tools without writing code. Ecom Swift LLC builds the triggers and actions, tests each step, writes the help content and prepares the connector for your customers.

## What is a no-code connector?

A no-code connector is an official bridge between your product and an automation platform such as Zapier or Make. It publishes a short menu of triggers, which start an automation when something happens in your product, and actions, which make your product do something. Customers pick them from a menu and connect them to other apps with a few clicks.

Examples are "new signup" as a trigger and "create a record" as an action.

## Why customers ask for it

Many of your customers are not developers, and they will never read API docs. They still want a new order to land in a spreadsheet, a new lead to alert their team chat or a new signup to join an email list. If your product cannot do this, they either ask your support team for help or leave for a tool that can.

A connector hands them the controls. Each customer builds their own automation, and you do not have to write a custom integration for each request.

## How a connector helps your product grow

The effect is easiest to see in retention and support. A product that fits into a customer's other tools becomes harder to replace, because workflows grow around it. Customers who automate routine steps use the product more often.

It also reduces custom work. Instead of building one-off links for every client, you offer one connector and let people assemble what they need. Templates make this easier: a ready-made automation shows a new user what is possible in the first minute.

## What a good connector contains

- Triggers for the events people care about, such as new order or updated contact.
- Actions for the tasks people want to automate, such as create or update a record.
- Secure sign-in so customers connect their own account safely.
- Sample data for every trigger, so the builder can map fields before real data arrives.
- Clear field names that a non-technical person understands.
- A tested path through each trigger and action inside the platform.
- A setup guide with screenshots for your help center.
- Example automations that customers can copy.
- Listing text and support page wording, when you want a public listing.

## What we do

We begin with your API and a short list of the events and tasks your customers ask for most. If your API is not ready or documented, we flag the gaps first. Then we build the connector, test every trigger and action inside the platform and fix field names that would confuse a newcomer.

The Basic package delivers a private connector with a few triggers and actions. Standard adds more of both, sign-in, a guide, example automations and preparation for a public listing review. Premium covers two platforms, ready-made templates, support page text and a handover call. Public listing approval is decided by the platform, so we prepare it but cannot promise the outcome.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Choose the five or six most useful events first.
- Name fields in everyday words.
- Provide realistic sample data.
- Test with a customer-style account, not an admin account.
- Publish a short guide next to the connector.

**Avoid:**
- Exposing every endpoint as an action.
- Using technical field names such as internal IDs only.
- Skipping error messages for failed steps.
- Launching without any example automation.
- Promising a listing date before the platform has reviewed it.

## Who it is for

A software company whose customers keep asking for a Zapier option needs a connector to point them to. A product team that wants its tool to appear next to popular apps in automation menus can use one. An agency can build a private connector for a client's internal automations.

## What we need from you

We need your API docs or access to a test environment, a list of the triggers and actions you want and a test account. Customers of the automation platform pay for their own plan, and you may need a developer account there, which we help you open. We work as a collaborator and never need passwords.
